newAbout.title: why did we invest in DayMoon?
newAbout.content:
Our decision to invest in DayMoon rests on three pillars: a large market that remains almost entirely unprotected, a distribution model built around companies that need to protect sensitive information, and a team built for this problem. DayMoon reduces the damage caused by phone theft. It combines an app that locks sensitive apps, such as banking, whenever the phone is away from trusted locations, with a human response center that acts on the victim's behalf right after the theft: locking the device, contacting each bank and carrier and warning family members against follow-up scams.


Phone theft is part of everyday life in Brazil. Around 13.9 million people had their phone stolen in the last twelve months, and nearly 8 in 10 fear it will happen to them. Yet very few are protected: phone insurance covers only about 4% of the devices in use, and less than half of victims manage to block their SIM card and device. The willingness to pay is already visible. With a no-code MVP and no marketing budget, the founders reached around 100 paying users in just over a month.


This problem goes beyond individuals. Many professionals work on their personal phones, which hold client emails, documents and conversations. For law firms, consultancies and other businesses that handle sensitive information, a stolen phone is not only a problem for the employee but a risk to their clients' confidentiality and to the firm's reputation. That is where we see DayMoon's main growth path: companies offering the service to their teams to protect both. There is international precedent for this model: in 2018, Allstate paid US$525 million for InfoArmor, an identity protection service distributed as a corporate benefit. Beyond employers, insurers that cover post-theft fraud are a natural complementary channel.


Executing this vision requires a team that combines security, partnerships and technology, and DayMoon has all three. Daniel Rozemberg brings years of hands-on security experience, including six years as Head of Security at FISESP, and designs the response protocol at the core of the product. Gabriel Koziner has already built and scaled a company, and leads the partnerships that will drive DayMoon's growth. CTO Daniel Vofchuk founded a software house and has built real-time tracking systems, the kind of fast and reliable technology that post-theft response depends on.


Every year, millions of Brazilians lose their phone and, with it, access to their money, their accounts and their peace of mind. The tools to lock a phone already exist. What DayMoon offers is someone who acts for the victim when it matters most. We believe this team can make DayMoon the standard for post-theft response in Brazil, and we are proud to be part of that journey.
